A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combination of ezetimibe with a statin was more effective than rosuvastatin alone in patients with hyperlipidemia, and that ezetimibe was more effective in patients who had been treated previously with higher potency statin doses.

the Ezetimibe/SIMVA 10/20mg combination therapy is more effective at lowering LDL-C and other lipid levels in patients who were previously on high potency statins compared to those on lower potency statins.
ezetimibe/simvastatin is superior to rosuvastatin in lowering cholesterol in patients on high-dose statins and is superior to rosuva in patients on low-dose statins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patients with prior statin treatment can benefit from switching to Ezetimibe/SIMVASTATIN 10/20mg.
patients on higher potency statins will benefit the most from switching to Ezetimibe/SIMVA, which will allow them to reach their LDL-C target more effectively.

patients with high risk for cardiovascular disease and who are already on statin therapy, can benefit from adding ezetimibe/simvastatin, compared to rosuvastatin alone, in terms of achieving lipid targets, including low-density lipoproteins, non-HDL cholesterol and apolipoproteins.
